findings.finding: JKArray.data is allocated by malloc at line255. The allocator function does not explicitly clear the entire data allocation; LOCATE clears only each first-seen output tile. This describes source-visible writes, not libc/OS allocation behavior.

The 400000000-double budget is divided by n_dm. Each OpenMP thread allocates n_dm JKArray.data buffers plus a separate integral/cache buffer. Thus the approximately3.2GB nominal reserve is per thread across the density buffers, not3.2GB per density; padding, metadata and allocator overhead are additional.

Within one write-back epoch, each block-pair key is allocated and cleared only while its outptr is NOVALUE. Write-back resets each used key and resets stack_size/key_counts. Later epochs may touch the same tile again.

For the reviewed full-AO output operators with matching disjoint AO block partitions, unique output tiles cover a subset of nbra*nket entries. Each JKArray.data stack high-water mark is therefore at most ncomp*nbra*nket doubles, at most ncomp*nao^2 for full762-AO output. Every epoch reuses the same data prefix.
The pragma has no num_threads(4). The four-thread arithmetic is conditional on an external runtime setting actually limiting this OpenMP team to at most4 threads; no live thread count was measured.

The nonhybrid gradient requests get_j. One2D density and one J script reach the direct driver with n_dm=1, and the gradient call passes ncomp=3. The762-AO dimension is a task-supplied current-system dimension, not recomputed by this audit.

The private payload bound excludes shared output matrices, reordered density matrices, integral/cache buffers, outptr/keys metadata, Python/BLAS/allocator state, physical-page rounding and huge-page effects. It also excludes GGA numerical-grid and CPHF xs/ax history memory.

bound_conditions: FullAO762-by762 output for the reviewed standard J operators.
Each output-axis uses the matching disjoint AO block partition.
n_dm counts actual driver operator/density entries, including any script replication.
Only one concurrently active direct-driver team is covered.
Four-thread totals require actual team size at most4.
The CPHF24-density case is a requested scenario, not an observed native call in this audit.

reserve_arithmetic.note: Nominal values are not exact allocated bytes. Total data and buf malloc bytes per thread equal8*(n_dm*size_limit+n_dm*136^2+di^4*ncomp+2*di^2+cache_size), plus metadata/allocator overhead. No integral/cache-size query was executed.

conclusion.statement: A nominal12.8GB virtual reserve for four native threads does not imply12.8GB resident payload. Conversely the55.74MB/445.93MB private payload figures are not totalRSS or physical-page bounds. Virtual-address/commit limits may still reject malloc, and GGA/CPHF history/other live arrays require separate budgets.

independent_read_only_review: A second agent independently checked allocation/LOCATE/write-back control flow and exact integer arithmetic, and required the epoch/thread-count/RSS qualifications recorded here.
